steps.prompt: What is the units digit of $2^{2026} + 3^{2026}$? Which digits of each number do you actually need?

cards.title: Only the last digit matters
cards.body: The units digit of a sum or product depends only on the units digits of the numbers: $17^{17}$ ends like $7^{17}$. The units digit is the remainder mod $10$. Powers cycle: $2$: $2, 4, 8, 6$; $3$: $3, 9, 7, 1$; $4$: $4, 6$; $7$: $7, 9, 3, 1$; $8$: $8, 4, 2, 6$; $9$: $9, 1$; and $0, 1, 5, 6$ never change.

cards.title: Worked example: a sum of powers
cards.problem: What is the units digit of $2^{2026} + 3^{2026}$?

steps.text: Both cycles have length $4$, and $2026 = 4 \times 506 + 2$: remainder $2$.

try.prompt: What is the remainder when $2026$ is divided by $4$?
What is the units digit of $3^{2026}$?
What is the units digit of $2^{2026} + 3^{2026}$?

cards.title: Big bases
cards.body: For $17^{17}$, drop everything but the last digit of the base: $7^{17}$. Then use the cycle of $7$ with the exponent's remainder mod $4$. Remainder $0$ means the LAST digit in the cycle (for $7$, that is $1$).

cards.title: Worked example: a big base
cards.problem: What is the units digit of $17^{17}$?

try.prompt: What is the remainder when $17$ is divided by $4$?

steps.text: Remainder $1$: the first digit of the cycle $7, 9, 3, 1$. The units digit is $7$.

try.prompt: What is the units digit of $17^{17}$?

cards.title: The common trap: the wrong cycle position
cards.body: Use the remainder of the EXPONENT mod the cycle length, not of the base. Remainder $0$ is the end of the cycle, not the start. For differences like $19^{19} - 11^{11}$, if the first units digit is smaller, borrow: $3 - 7$ ends in $6$.
